basis: Defined by ovarian and testicular tissue and reproductive tract differences; no endocrine dysfunction or urinary tract damage established.
Congenital skeletal muscle disease with nemaline bodies; respiratory insufficiency is occasional and reflects muscle weakness.
Defined by peripheral nerve injury and persistent neuropathic dysfunction; edema and vasomotor changes do not establish separate skin or vascular damage.
Usually an isolated nail disorder; annotated kidney stones and blepharitis are separate associated diseases, not direct damage from leukonychia.
Bone neoplasm arising from notochordal remnants; adjacent neural compression is not established across this umbrella.
Gonococcal infection of reproductive organs; testicular inflammation alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Diffuse neoplastic overgrowth of adipose tissue, including subcutis; associated liver disease and treatment exposures are not direct organ involvement.
Axial skeletal dysplasia with osteosclerosis and vertebral abnormalities; occasional nonspecific metabolic findings do not establish a metabolic disorder.
Progressive inherited retinal dysfunction with night blindness and visual loss; hearing impairment is occasional (5-29%).
Progeroid lipodystrophy and muscle/skeletal abnormalities define the phenotype; cataract in 1/3; hepatocellular carcinoma is a separate predisposed malignancy.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; hearing loss 2/3, hypodontia 2/5 and persistent esodeviation 1/3 support additional organs, though samples are small.
Congenital intestinal secretory dysfunction; subtype-specific electrolyte disorders do not establish an independent metabolic axis across the umbrella.
Adenocarcinoma originating in the extrahepatic bile duct, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Defined as nonsyndromic intellectual disability; flat feet in 4/4 and bifid uvula in 1/3 lack documented functional damage to additional organs.
Mesenchymal soft tissue tumor usually arising in the extremities; no common direct involvement of additional organs established.
Oral hamartomas and limb dysplasia define syndrome; developmental impairment and hearing loss each 80-99%; airway and ocular abnormalities omitted by cap.
Polyamine disorder with brain abnormalities and alopecia; ptosis in 2/4 and frequent annotations; hearing loss reported in only 1 assessed patient, prevalence uncertain.
Loss of cerebral visual shape processing; the deficit does not establish disease of the eyes themselves.
Defined by congenital muscular dystrophy with brain and eye malformations; retinal dysplasia in 2/4; renal dysplasia in 1/4 is below threshold.
Myopathy and skeletal abnormalities with defining cardiac disease; ventricular hypertrophy and mitral regurgitation each 2/3; transaminases do not prove liver damage.
Deafness and skin/hair pigmentation abnormalities define syndrome; iris heterochromia does not impair vision; bowel and peripheral nerve disease are subtype-limited.
Tumor originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish origin in locomotor muscle.
SCN1A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures, ataxia and cognitive impairment reflect nervous system dysfunction.
Intellectual disability and hypogonadism define syndrome; toe contractures/short digits 80-99%, ptosis/blepharophimosis 30-79%; sparse hair omitted by cap.
Niacin deficiency causes persistent dermatitis and gastrointestinal mucosal injury; dementia, delirium and cognitive impairment are frequent (30-79%).
